findings.statement: Coinbase's official product materials confirm XRP-backed USDC loans through Morpho on Base and explicitly require cbXRP on Base when adding collateral to an XRP loan.
findings.disconfirming_evidence: No official Coinbase disclosure in this run identifies the exact market ID or the fraction of market activity generated through its interface.

findings.statement: Morpho market 0xd4a903…6e4109 is the likely primary market behind Coinbase's XRP loan product: it is the cbXRP/USDC Base market, uses 62.5% LLTV, predates the Coinbase XRP-loan expansion and is identified as such by an independent Morpho-data project. The market is permissionless, so not all market volume belongs to Coinbase customers.
findings.disconfirming_evidence: No official Coinbase market-ID mapping or Coinbase-only borrower/volume disclosure.

findings.statement: At 00:31 UTC the market-data snapshot reports $59.11M USDC borrowed against 118.46M cbXRP valued at $148.9M, 90.4% utilization and 62.5% LLTV. It also reports 1,120 liquidations in 30 days and $3.94M debt repaid.
findings.disconfirming_evidence: Market-wide third-party API-derived values; Morpho app liquidity/utilization fields differ and need block-consistent reconciliation.

findings.statement: Circle issues native USDC on Base and on XRPL. USDC is the debt asset in the cbXRP/USDC Morpho market; no direct Circle lender role or Base↔XRPL bridge flow was established.
findings.disconfirming_evidence: No Circle market-supply address or cross-chain transfer route was identified.

findings.statement: Coinbase's published cbXRP reserve page lists 20 XRPL reserve addresses and 151,405,263.6 XRP against 151,403,016.069 cbXRP. The 20 addresses have zero exact matches with the five Binance incident source wallets.
findings.disconfirming_evidence: Coinbase's reserve page is first-party and not an independent audit; zero exact address overlap does not rule out indirect flows or common beneficial control.

findings.statement: The collateralized-loan rail may reduce forced sales by allowing some XRP holders to borrow USDC while retaining exposure, but the same structure creates a conditional liquidation channel during drawdowns. Neither net XRP demand nor forced XRP spot selling is demonstrated.
findings.disconfirming_evidence: Loan proceeds are reportedly barred from Coinbase trading; no onchain trace from borrowed USDC to XRP purchases or from cbXRP liquidation to native XRP sales was established.

findings.statement: Coinbase's share of the permissionless cbXRP/USDC market, Circle's direct USDC lending exposure, and the ultimate beneficial source of vault deposits remain unknown.
findings.disconfirming_evidence: None; the available sources do not disclose these allocations.

market_observations.notes: Market-wide permissionless data; not Coinbase customer-only. 20% downside risk is collateral at risk, not expected liquidation or spot sale.
Morpho app reports $15.31M total liquidity, $74.47M market size and 91.67% utilization; those values are not arithmetically consistent and are excluded.
Coinbase says reserve may exceed supply due to timing differences, delayed transactions, fees or operational movements; not an independent audit.
Vault allocation is not ultimate beneficial-depositor concentration and does not establish Circle as a lender.

competing_hypotheses.claim: The 62.5% cbXRP/USDC Morpho market is the principal market accessed by Coinbase's XRP-backed loan interface.
supporting_evidence: Coinbase confirms XRP loans use Morpho on Base and requires cbXRP on Base as collateral.
Morpho market is cbXRP/USDC on Base with 62.5% LLTV and was created January 15, 2026, before Coinbase's February 18 XRP-loan expansion.
Morpho Watch independently identifies it as the market behind Coinbase XRP loans.
disconfirming_evidence: Morpho market is permissionless and can be accessed outside Coinbase.
Coinbase does not publish a market ID or channel-level customer volume.
unknowns: Coinbase UI share of total market borrowing.
Whether Coinbase customers use other cbXRP markets or direct Morpho routes.

competing_hypotheses.claim: cbXRP collateralized borrowing can reduce the need for some XRP holders to sell existing XRP to raise liquidity, but does not establish incremental XRP purchases.
supporting_evidence: Coinbase markets the product as borrowing USDC without selling XRP.
cbXRP is locked on Morpho while underlying XRP remains in Coinbase custody.
disconfirming_evidence: Loan proceeds cannot be used to trade on Coinbase under reported product terms.
No traced USDC-to-XRP purchase flow was found.
Borrowers may use proceeds for consumption, debt repayment, other assets or external venues.
unknowns: Counterfactual amount of XRP that would otherwise have been sold.

competing_hypotheses.claim: cbXRP liquidations can create a Base-side sell-pressure channel that may reach native XRP only if liquidators redeem or transfer the wrapped asset through Coinbase.
supporting_evidence: Market has 62.5% LLTV, 12.68% bonus, 1,120 liquidations and $3.94M debt repaid over 30 days.
Approximately $21.48M collateral is estimated at risk under a 20% cbXRP decline.
disconfirming_evidence: Morpho app displays zero realized and unrealized bad debt.
No complete liquidation→cbXRP sale→unwrap→XRPL/CEX sale path was traced.
Risk-at-price-decline is not an expected liquidation amount.
unknowns: Coinbase unwrap/redemption latency and resulting XRP transfers.
Actual slippage and pool depth at liquidation times.

competing_hypotheses.claim: Circle's USDC is a core debt asset in this XRP collateral rail, but Circle is not shown to be the lender or collateral custodian.
supporting_evidence: Morpho market loan asset is USDC on Base.
Circle officially supports native USDC on Base and XRPL.
Vault allocations are listed under Steakhouse, Clearstar, K3, Gauntlet and Yearn.
disconfirming_evidence: No Circle treasury or Circle Mint address was identified as a direct market supplier in this review.
Vault underlying depositor identities are not fully observable from the aggregate table.
unknowns: Beneficial source of USDC deposits into vaults.
Any direct Circle market-making or lending allocation.

competing_hypotheses.claim: USDC supply concentration and high market utilization create a liquidity/rate sensitivity even when borrower positions are numerous.
supporting_evidence: Morpho Watch reports 90.4% utilization and $6.31M available against $59.11M borrowed.
Top three listed vaults allocate $52.28M, about 79.9% of reported market supply.
Variable borrowing rates rise as utilization exceeds the 90% target.
disconfirming_evidence: Additional vault liquidity may be allocated; the page estimates up to $7.18M available including allocator capacity.
Morpho app liquidity fields do not reconcile with the aggregator snapshot.
unknowns: Block-consistent free liquidity and withdrawal queue behavior.

competing_hypotheses.claim: The Coinbase cbXRP reserve is separate from the Binance incident wallet cluster and should not be treated as exchange tradable float.
supporting_evidence: Coinbase publishes 20 cbXRP backing addresses and a 1:1 reserve/supply table.
None of the five Binance incident source addresses exactly matches the Coinbase reserve set.
Coinbase says underlying wrapped-asset backing is not sold, transferred or used for other purposes.
disconfirming_evidence: Coinbase page is self-reported and not an independent audit.
Zero exact overlap does not rule out historical transfers or shared beneficial control.
unknowns: Independent direct Base totalSupply and XRP reserve address balance verification at one block cutoff.
Any indirect historical flow between exchange clusters.

relationship_edges.details: Coinbase provides the borrower interface; Morpho holds collateral and executes the onchain lending market.
Coinbase's official product material includes XRP among supported collateral assets.
Coinbase's backup collateral table maps XRP loans to cbXRP on Base at contract 0xcb585250f852c6c6bf90434ab21a00f02833a4af.
Published reserve 151,405,263.6 XRP backs 151,403,016.069 cbXRP across 20 listed XRPL addresses; underlying backing is stated not to be sold, transferred or used for another purpose.
The market pairs cbXRP collateral with USDC debt and has a fixed 62.5% LLTV.
Market-wide borrowed amount is approximately $59.1M at the 00:31 UTC snapshot.
Circle Mint and APIs support native USDC on Base; Circle is the loan-asset issuer, not thereby a lender to this market.
USDC is also natively available on XRPL; this separate deployment does not establish a direct Base↔XRPL transfer route.

relationship_edges.from_entity: Steakhouse, Clearstar, K3, Gauntlet and Yearn vaults
relationship_edges.details: Nine listed vaults provide $58.56M of $65.42M supplied; top three provide $52.28M, approximately 79.9% of total market supply.
Morpho app lists ChainlinkOracleV2, 1-day heartbeat and 0.5% deviation for the collateral price feed.
The market displays a 12.67–12.68% liquidation bonus; this is distinct from Coinbase Help's unresolved 4.38% penalty statement.
This limits claims that the loan product mechanically generates Coinbase spot XRP buying.
No exact address match; this does not rule out indirect ownership or historical transfers.

next_actions: Reconcile Morpho market supply, borrow, available liquidity, utilization and rates from one block-consistent public API snapshot; resolve Morpho app/aggregator field differences.
Obtain the exact Coinbase UI-to-Morpho market mapping and distinguish Coinbase-originated borrowers from permissionless direct users without inferring identity from wallet heuristics.
Build 30/90-day immutable series for cbXRP supply, Morpho borrow, collateral, vault allocation, rates, liquidations and Base DEX depth.
Trace sampled liquidation transactions from Morpho collateral seizure through cbXRP DEX sale, Coinbase redemption and any XRPL/CEX transfer; do not assume the full chain.
Clarify the Coinbase 4.38% penalty versus Morpho 12.67–12.68% liquidation bonus and the generic 86% note versus the market-specific 62.5% LLTV.
Identify vault-level USDC suppliers only from public, attributable records; do not attribute vault capital to Circle without direct evidence.
Keep all collateral and stablecoin measures out of price-prediction features until point-in-time history, data-quality checks, leakage controls and walk-forward tests pass.
